item.title: Manu Ginobili's signed, game-worn Nikes score big at auction
item.description: Top bid throwback: a signed, game-used pair of Manu Ginobili Nike Air Uptempo player-exclusive sneakers worn by the Spurs star 20 years ago. (Courtesy Goldin) When is a Manu Ginobili autograph worth more than $9,000? When it's Sharpie'd on a pair of shoes the Spurs great wore 20 years ago. A twice-signed pair of Ginobili game-used Nike Air Uptempo Pro player exclusive sneakers recently sold at auction at Goldin for $9,394. The winning bid clocked in at $7,700, but the price spikes with the buyer's premium fee at 22% of the final bid price. The player-exclusive Manu Ginobili Nike Air Uptempos feature the Spurs star's autograph and jersey number. Ginobili wore the sneakers for two games in 2006. (Courtesy Goldin) Manu Ginobili signed the toebox of both sneakers. (Courtesy Goldin) The black kicks with the silver swoosh feature Ginobili's signature monogram "MG" logo on the tongue and his jersey No. 20 on the heels. Ginobili signed each sneaker inside the toebox with silver ink. Of course, that was after he laced them up for a couple of West Coast wins in 2006. Gotta be the Manu shoes. (Jeff Gross/Getty Images) The sneakers were photo-matched to two games Ginobili played with the Spurs in Los Angeles at what was then called the Staples Center: a 98-87 win against the Clippers on March 28 and a 96-85 win against the Lakers two nights later. ZOUNDS: Texan pulls Spurs star Dylan Harper's rookie card valued at nearly $3 million Spurs great Manu Ginobili handles the ball against the Los Angeles Clippers on March 28, 2006, at Staples Center in Los Angeles, Calif. Two decades later, the shoes he wore for the game would sell for $9,000. (Jeff Gross/Getty Images) Spurs star Manu Ginobili puts up a shot as the Los Angeles Lakers' Kobe Bryant, left, Lamar Odom (7), and Brian Cook, right, guard during the first half of the NBA basketball game March 30, 2006, in Los Angeles. Ginobili wore the same shoes as he did two nights prior against the Clippers. (MARK J. TERRILL/AP) In the Clippers game, Ginobili scored eight points with a game-high nine assists and three steals. Against the Lakers, he racked up 11 points, four assists, a couple of rebounds and a game-high three steals. The shoes have the wear to show it. According to the auction description, the Nikes sported game use and aging, including creasing, emblem yellowing, loose stitching and scuff marks. The sold sneakers came with a MeiGray letter of authenticity confirming game use and Beckett letters of authenticity for the signatures. No word if they also came with a pair of Sneaker Balls. item.title: AEW Full Gear predictions: 5 big questions as Will Ospreay vs. Kyle Fletcher, Anarchy in the Arena await
item.description: AEW Full Gear 2026 , one of the promotion's original pay-per-view franchises, takes place this weekend in Phoenix, Arizona. Featuring at least six championship matches and the annual Anarchy in the Arena brawl, Full Gear looks to continue an impressive 2026 run for Tony Khan's wrestling promotion. With such a loaded card on deck, the Uncrowned Horsemen — Kel Dansby, Robert Jackman, Drake Riggs and Anthony Sulla-Heffinger — are here to break down the event and make predictions for one of the last major AEW events of 2026. Let's ride! 1. Kyle Fletcher and Will Ospreay have a long history together. What's made their rivalry work so well, and where does it go from here? Can it become an all-time AEW rivalry? Jackman: Like other longstanding wrestling partnerships, I think what gives this one the extra oomph is that both men have such a deep personal connection — that they've been friends, as well as opponents and on-off teammates, since the first time they wrestled in front of a crowd, and have since gone on to support each other in making the jump to the big leagues, both in Japan and of course AEW. I mean, they even lived together in Tokyo. When you listen to what we purists call "shoot" interviews, it's clear they have a hell of a lot of trust in each other's abilities. They also both come across as self-critical types who would probably push each other on toward the next level. It's the sort of friendship that will make both men better wrestlers for it. As for what's transpired in AEW, the secret sauce for me has been this long, ongoing thread of the Don Callis Family. You have all the elements of a deep-cut rivalry in there: The fact that Ospreay piggybacked off the Callis Family for a while, only to leave them behind when he decided to be a good guy — whereas Fletcher has stayed in the fold and learned that extra killer instinct from it. It's that same killer instinct that I predict will lead to Fletcher eventually dethroning his real-life bestie — just not this weekend. As for an all-time rivalry, it's basically one rung below Swerve and "Hangman" at the moment. Sulla-Heffinger: The beauty of this rivalry is that their styles and skill set are so similar that it's almost impossible for them not to have excellent chemistry. Nearly every time these two have shared a ring against each other in AEW, it's been in the conversation for Match of the Year. I think from a storytelling standpoint, I equate this to what we've seen play out between Roman Reigns and Seth Rollins in WWE, albeit over a significantly shorter length of time. There are obvious parallels to be made considering Fletcher's closeness with Ospreay in the United Empire and his eventual betrayal of "The Aerial Assassin." With so much history, unmatched skill sets and the fact that both are so young, there's plenty of runway for them to make this the defining men's rivalry of AEW. item.description: Floodlights over the Losail circuit in Qatar during a 2010 MotoGP weekend. Illustrative image, not from this year's races. Photo: daly3d abd from Qatar, Doha via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0) With Imola stood down, Formula 1’s 2026 season is still set to finish in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. According to reports from PlanetF1 , The Race and RacingNews365 , F1 told the Italian circuit on Tuesday that it would not be needed as a backup finale. Today’s confirmed news adds one driver announcement: Racing Bulls will keep Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad for 2027. Schedules and announcements below come from formula1.com, the FIA, the circuit organizers and MotoGP’s official site, checked on Nov. 12. Anything that rests on press reports rather than an official statement is labeled that way. The one storyline: Imola is stood down, and the Gulf finale is on Here is what is reported. F1 told Imola it would not host a replacement finale, and informed teams that Qatar (race day Sunday, Nov. 29, at Lusail) and Abu Dhabi (Sunday, Dec. 6, at Yas Marina) stay on the calendar. Imola had been held in reserve for a December 4 to 6 event. PlanetF1 reports that F1 said it could not keep the circuit on standby indefinitely and will cover the costs of the preparations made so far. Here is what is still open. All three outlets paraphrase the decision, and I could not find a full statement on formula1.com, so treat the details as reported. The Race says F1 is reviewing threat assessments “on an hourly basis” and would not hesitate to pull the plug if the risk became unnecessary. RacingNews365 adds that the call is not final and that F1 will act if the situation worsens. On the FIA side, president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said earlier this week that both races will go ahead, as we covered in Tuesday’s briefing . That briefing said F1 had not yet confirmed the finale. These reports, published later the same day, change that picture. The pit lane at Imola during first practice for the 2025 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix. Illustrative image; Imola has now been stood down as a 2026 finale backup. Photo: Jmmuguerza via Wikimedia Commons ( CC BY-SA 4.0 ) Analysis: standing Imola down removes the safety net, and that is the real change. Until now, a cancellation in the Gulf had somewhere to go. From here, any late change would mean a shortened season, not a swap. item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Sacramento, California, USA; Memphis Grizzlies guard-forward Ty Jerome (2) reacts after making a basket against the Sacramento Kings during the fourth quarter at Golden 1 Center. Mandatory Credit: Dennis Lee-Imagn Images What a wild start to the 2026-27 NBA season. If you looked at the preseason expectations for the Most Improved Player award, you can throw that idea right in the bin, because reality turned out completely different. Most teams have only played about 10 to 12 games, so we are dealing with small sample sizes, but that is honestly what makes it so much fun. The MIP award is always tricky to predict. Some guys make a massive jump by going from scoring 10 points to 20 points a night, while others completely change their style while helping their teams win actual games. Instead of the usual lottery picks taking normal steps forward, we are seeing bench players turn into stars, younger guards shoot the lights out, and veterans reinvent themselves entirely. As we wrap up Week 3, the landscape is moving fast. An 82-game season is a long marathon, and injuries, fatigue, and scouting adjustments are coming. But right now, these 10 guys have grabbed our attention and completely flipped their season around. Let’s dive right into our updated power rankings, starting from No. 10. 10. Jabari Smith Jr., Houston Rockets 2025-26 Stats: 15.8 PPG, 6.9 RPG, 1.9 APG, 45.0 FG%, 36.3 3P% 2026-27 Stats: 17.0 PPG, 6.5 RPG, 2.4 APG, 50.4 FG%, 44.8 3P% Jabari Smith Jr. isn’t making the massive scoring jump that some of the other guys on this list are showing, but what he is doing with his shooting efficiency is incredible. Entering his fourth year in the league, the former No. 3 overall pick is finally unlocking the pure shooting potential that everyone knew he had. Right now, Smith is putting up 17.0 points per game for a very solid Houston Rockets team. Bumping your average up by just 1.2 points from last year’s 15.8 doesn’t sound like a crazy MIP resume on paper. But look closer at how he is scoring. His field-goal percentage has jumped to 50.4%, and his three-point percentage is sitting at a scorching 44.8%. For a stretch-four whose main job is to space the floor and defend, hitting nearly 45% of your threes changes everything for the Rockets’ offense. He is splashing 2.7 triples a night compared to 2.3 last year, and get this: he is doing it while taking fewer total shots (down from 12.6 to 11.9 attempts). That is incredible efficiency. His true shooting percentage jumped from 57.0% all the way to 65.0%. The only reason he is down at No. 10 is the raw numbers. Voters love big counting stats, and his rebounding has actually dipped a tiny bit to 6.5 boards. If he can push that scoring average past 20 points while keeping up this crazy shooting, he will climb these rankings fast. 9. item.title: Stephen A. Smith says what the Vikings have done to one of their players is a ‘disgrace’
item.description: Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings made their move before the trade deadline to bring in Kirk Cousins as their new quarterback. Kevin O’Connell decided that heading into the remainder of the season with Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz as his options at QB was not going to help their hopes of making it to the Super Bowl. Although a move for Cousins was widely viewed as a positive, it also highlighted the mess created by the Vikings over recent years. Stephen A. Smith is one of those people who have come down heavily on the Vikings for not looking after the quarterback position in recent years. The constant changes at the position have been criticised by Smith, who admits he feels sorry for Justin Jefferson. Stephen A. Smith defends Justin Jefferson amid the Minnesota Vikings’ quarterback mess Ever since allowing Sam Darnold to depart the building, Jefferson’s production has declined, with only two touchdowns to his name throughout the entire 2025 season. Jefferson has already surpassed that with four touchdowns this season, but his 393 receiving yards is nothing in comparison to league leader Jaxon Smith-Njigba (1,036). “Well, we have every reason to believe that this week he’s going to start looking like the receiver we know him to be, at least to some degree. It was an utter disgrace what the Minnesota Vikings have done to him. I called out Kevin O’Connell yesterday, and I meant every word of it. It’s a shame what they’ve done to Justin Jefferson over the last year and a half,” Smith said on First Take. “You don’t have an all-world receiver like that. He hasn’t looked like that over the last year and a half because he hasn’t had a quarterback in the history of the National Football League. I am guaranteeing that everybody is going to agree with the statement that I’m about to make. “There is no wide receiver that has ever been successful throwing the football to himself. It has never happened. You can’t throw the football to yourself.” The Vikings’ defense has been operating at an extremely high level this season, but the offense has been unable to hold its end of the bargain. Being unable to extract the best out of Jefferson has been a major failure for the organization, as they have messed around at the quarterback position. There will now be hope that bringing Cousins back to Minnesota will bring some consistency back to the position and help Jefferson get back to doing what he does best. item.title: Lonzo Ball says which NBA team has the ugliest fans
item.description: Photo by Tyler Clouse/Getty Images Lonzo Ball has just damaged his chances of ever signing with one NBA team. Lonzo Ball is in a pretty interesting spot in his career right now. Sitting on the open market as a free agent, the former number two overall pick is still looking for a new NBA team to give him a shot and let him prove he can stay healthy on the floor. While he waits for the right deal to come along, Ball has been staying busy off the court by leaning into his podcast and media work. However, all that extra time behind a microphone has definitely kept him in the headlines, even if roasting Memphis fans wasn’t on anyone’s bingo card. Lonzo Ball calls Memphis Grizzlies fans the ugliest in the NBA Lonzo Ball clearly isn’t worried about making friends in Tennessee anytime soon. Speaking on NBAT2 around seven months ago, he bluntly named Memphis as the city with the ugliest fans in the league. He said: “I don’t want to say Memphis because I f*** with people from Memphis, but that was the first city that popped into my mind. If you’re going to go somewhere, I wouldn’t suggest you go to Memphis first.” Ball looked like he was finally putting everything together in Chicago, thriving as a two-way playmaker alongside Zach LaVine and DeMar DeRozan. However, things fell apart in January 2022, though, when a torn meniscus turned into a brutal string of knee surgeries, including a rare cartilage transplant, that sidelined him for more than two full seasons. Those constant setbacks wiped out his momentum and led to him struggling with the Cleveland Cavaliers before being waived. item.title: Trae Young’s Early-Season Slump Could Become A Major Problem For The Wizards
item.description: Oct 28, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Washington Wizards guard Trae Young (3) reacts in the first quarter against the Cleveland Cavaliers at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images The Washington Wizards accumulated some interesting talent ahead of the new campaign . With the arrival of Trae Young and Anthony Davis , the Wizards were on the verge of ushering in a new era led by two superstars . Now, 12 games into the 2026-27 season, however, Washington may need to revisit its plans. Despite the talent at their disposal, the Washington Wizards have struggled to establish themselves as a playoff team. Following their latest 114-101 loss to the Indiana Pacers , their fifth consecutive one, the Wizards have slid down the Eastern Conference leaderboard, landing up in 12th place with a 4-8 record. In many ways, calling this situation a disaster may be an exaggeration. Given how impactful Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa have been during this period, there are some positive takeaways to build on. However, concerns about Trae Young’s form should not be overlooked. At the time of his arrival, Trae Young was expected to be the floor general who could bring out the best in Washington’s players. Given his track record, which includes four All-Star appearances, an All-NBA appearance, and an assists title in the 2024-25 season, Young had the accomplishments to support this. Sadly, this season has started off on a bad note for the 28-year-old. In 12 appearances thus far, Young is averaging 18.3 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 8.3 assists per game, which seems okay on paper. However, when factoring in his shooting splits of 40.0% from the field and an underwhelming 29.6% from three-point range, there is clearly much to be desired. With career averages of 24.9 points and 9.7 assists per game, Young is clearly falling short of expectations. However, as a career 35.0% shooter from deep, his current efficiency from the perimeter, especially in light of Washington’s 29.8% shooting from beyond the arc (29th in the NBA) as a team, is alarming. Is Trae Young The Odd Man Out? On the face of it, Trae Young has the tools and the ability to be one of the best floor generals in the NBA. Despite his size, Young’s creativity as a ball-handler and playmaker is on par with some of the best. When specifically referring to his ability to create scoring chances in pick-and-roll situations, Young is arguably the best in the league. So what exactly is going wrong for the 28-year-old? Given the quality of big men in Washington, which includes the likes of Anthony Davis, Alex Sarr, and Deandre Ayton among others, Trae Young should be thriving in pick-and-roll sets. item.title: Cowboys escape Colts but familiar problems continue to haunt Dallas
item.description: The Cowboys may have walked away with a 27-23 victory over the Colts but that doesn't mean all is well in Dallas. Getting back to the win column provided some much-needed relief, yet questions remain about whether this team is actually making meaningful progress or simply avoiding disappointing results. In what should have been a comfortable victory instead turned into an uncomfortable afternoon, forcing the Cowboys to rally late against an opponent that has little reason to believe in their own season. This weeks winners and losers list has an odd feel to it as optimism remains possible, but confidence is increasingly difficult to justify. There lies a strange reality in Dallas as several performances deserve recognition, while others serve as reminders that victory doesn't suddenly fix everything in Dallas. Winner WR CeeDee Lamb Wideout CeeDee Lamb continues his assault on the Cowboys record books after catching 10 passes for 195 yards and touchdown against two-time All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner and the Indianapolis Colts secondary. Through nine games, Lamb has 70 receptions for 904 yards and seven touchdowns. He is on pace for 132 receptions for 1,707 yards. Lamb already has the most receptions in Cowboys history with 135 in 2023. That same season, he posted 1,749 yards which is also most in team history. item.title: Paudie O’Connor Is Your October 2026 Player Of The Month
item.description: It’s not too often we get a surprise winner for our Player of the Month awards. I really thought October’s would go to Kyreece Lisbie, who led the way in the scoring charts with four goals (two braces)… but nope. Congratulations instead to Paudie O’Connor , who came out on top in a well contested vote . He led the way with 37%, as Paddy Lane (27%) edged out Lisbie (24%) to take second. Udoka Godwin-Malife earned a respectable 11% in fourth spot. In truth, all would have been worthy winners. Though October was an eclectic month overall for results and performances, we can’t say there weren’t standout individuals. O’Connor’s defensive displays shone the most brightly for you, however. His contributions were vital in a run of one goal conceded in three games (Leyton Orient, Barnsley, Plymouth Argyle) that helped the Royals pick up seven points from the final nine possible in October. Though he was a candidate for Player of the Season last term ( finishing sixth behind Jack Marriott, Lewis Wing, Joel Pereira, Derrick Williams and Kamari Doyle), this is actually O’Connor’s first POTM award. He also picked up a first Man of the Match of this season at Home Park, so all in all it’s been a good few weeks for him. item.title: Full-back Barrett leads New Zealand for first time
item.description: Beauden Barrett was part of the 2015 New Zealand World Cup winning side [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Full-back Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time when he leads out the All Blacks for the Nations Championship game against Wales in Cardiff on Saturday. All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has made eight starting changes from the side that defeated Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield with 10 alterations in the match-day 23. It will be 35-year-old Barrett's first time as starting skipper in his 149th international with brother Scott also named at lock, while Richie Mo'unga is at fly-half. "Beauden brings such valuable experience and is massively respected by us all," said Rennie. "Captaining the All Blacks in a Test is an honour I know he doesn't take lightly, so it'll be a proud day for him and his whanau [family]." Basham starts for Wales as Wainwright ruled out Why Wales have a lot to prove despite beating Japan Smiling Rees-Zammit has no fear of All Blacks No Jordan for All Blacks in Cardiff The All Blacks defeated Scotland 43-21 last Saturday, but record try-scoring wing Will Jordan (hamstring) and centre Jordie Barratt (facial) picked up injuries and are absent against Wales. Flanker Anton Segner and wing Fehi Fineanganofo, whose move to Newcastle Red Bulls in the summer was delayed by a year, make their first Test starts. Segner, prop George Bower, hooker Asafo Aumua and scrum-half Cortez Ratima move from the replacements into the starting side. Mo'unga, Fineanganofo, lock Josh Lord and centre Anton Lienert-Brown also come into the side. "We have created good depth in this group and there is a lot of competition for places," said Rennie. "We have selected a strong squad with 783 caps." New Zealand have won the past 34 Tests against Wales in a winning sequence that stretches back to 1953. "Wales are a proud rugby nation and building nicely under Steve Tandy," said Rennie. "We are well aware of the threat they pose and the challenge of playing in front of a passionate crowd at Principality Stadium." item.title: ‘Did nothing for the fans’: Columnist says Tom Brady ‘no longer cares’ about Patriots
item.description: Tom Brady Tom Brady’s return to Foxborough last weekend was supposed to be a celebration. Instead, it has left plenty of people in Boston questioning his relationship with the city where he won six Super Bowls. Boston Globe columnist Ben Volin is the latest to rip the former Patriots quarterback. In a new column, Volin argued that it “has become painfully obvious that Tom Brady no longer cares about Boston, New England, or Patriots fans.” Brady’s Return to New England Brady was back in Foxborough over the weekend for Rob Gronkowski’s induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday. The next day, he called his first Patriots game for Fox, a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Brady had admitted that the return would be emotional , and he even poked fun at Drake Maye after the quarterback’s three-interception performance. But some in Boston felt that he went too easy on the Patriots during the broadcast. Brady’s relationship with Patriots fans was already tested in February, when he said that he had “no dog in the fight” during the Patriots’ Super Bowl run. ‘Like a piece of furniture’ In his column , Volin pointed to Brady’s appearance at Gronkowski’s induction, where Brady was introduced to chants from the crowd but did little more than wave. “He sat on stage for an hour like a piece of furniture, not participating,” Volin wrote. “Brady showed up for Gronkowski, but did nothing for the fans.” Volin contrasted Brady with Gronkowski, who has remained active in charity work across New England through the Gronk Nation Youth Foundation. Brady, meanwhile, has “seemingly cut off all ties” with the area since leaving in 2020, Volin argued. “When was the last time anyone said those things about Brady?” Volin wrote. Volin also took aim at Brady’s broadcast and his business ventures, including his minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders. He concluded that Brady may feel that his six Super Bowl titles are all he owes New England. “Brady sure acts like it,” Volin wrote. Needless to say, not everyone in New England is ready to give Brady a pass. item.title: Former Bills coach arrested after allegedly running over pedestrians' feet in hit-and-run
item.description: Former Buffalo Bills coach Rex Ryan was arrested Wednesday after police say he ran over two pedestrians' feet with his pickup truck in Nashville, argued with them when they confronted him and drove away. Ryan, 63, faces six misdemeanor charges stemming from the Nov. 5 incident, which left both pedestrians with minor injuries. According to the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department, the pedestrians were crossing Broadway with a walk signal shortly before midnight when Ryan allegedly turned right onto the street from Fourth Avenue, running over both pedestrians' feet and striking one person's leg. Police said Ryan continued driving before stopping at a red light, where the pedestrians caught up to him. The pedestrians told police Ryan got out of his truck and argued with them before getting back in and driving away. They photographed the driver and the truck's license plate, which police said was registered to Ryan. Ryan turned himself in to Nashville police Wednesday morning on six outstanding misdemeanor warrants. He is charged with two counts each of leaving the scene of an accident, failure to provide information or render aid, and failure to obey a traffic control signal. His bond was set at $6,000, but he qualified for release without posting bond. He is scheduled to appear in court in December. Ryan's attorney, David Raybin, told Nashville television station WSMV that Ryan turned himself in after learning of the allegations and is cooperating with the investigation. Ryan coached the Bills for two seasons from 2015 to 2016, compiling a 15-16 record before being fired with one game remaining in his second season. Buffalo went 8-8 in Ryan's first season and 7-8 in his second, missing the playoffs both years. Ryan previously coached the New York Jets for six seasons, leading them to consecutive AFC Championship Game appearances following the 2009 and 2010 seasons. He joined ESPN as an NFL analyst in 2017 and currently appears on "Sunday NFL Countdown." "We are aware and are in touch with Rex," ESPN said in a statement Wednesday. item.description: I don’t know about you, but the argument of “ he started it” never worked especially well for me. Parents don’t care, teachers don’t care, and in the case of Usman Nurmagomedov , the UFC should not care. On Wednesday, Nurmagomedov (cousin of MMA great Khabib) attacked UFC fighter Merab Dvalishvili at a hotel in Abu Dhabi, where the latter is due to wrestle this week . Nurmagomedov walked up behind Dvalishvili, who was being interviewed at the time, and as the Georgian turned to face him, the Russian slapped Dvalishvili, who was left visibly shocked. No, that does not justify Dvalishvili’s past act, but Nurmagomedov’s actions were similarly indefensible on Wednesday. Dvalishvili was held back by a friend, the only ally with him, who has since been identified as 21-year-old Saba Lazishvili. Another of Nurmagomedov’s companions punched Dvalishvili a fraction of a second later, at which point Lazishvili let him go, leading Dvalishvili to throw hands in a frenzied fashion. Nurmagomedov appeared to knee Dvalishvili in the face, before someone grabbed the Georgian from behind and slammed him face first onto the ground. item.title: Dan Hicks, legendary NBC Sports and golf announcer, dies at age 64
item.description: PONTE VEDRA BEACH, FLORIDA - MARCH 11: Dan Hicks poses for a photo during the NBC Golf Channel Broadcast during the third round of THE PLAYERS Championship at Stadium Course at TPC Sawgrass on March 11, 2023 in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida. (Photo by Ben Jared/PGA TOUR via Getty Images) PGA TOUR Legendary NBC Sports broadcaster Dan Hicks died Wednesday following an acute illness, his family said in a statement. He was 64. “Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan following an acute illness,” Hicks’ wife, Hannah Storm, said in a statement. “He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many. His loss is immeasurable. “Dan was truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around. When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter and the people together. He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered. “Our three daughters and I are heartbroken. We are grateful for the love and support surrounding our family during this incredibly difficult time. These are simply no words to express how much he will be missed.” Hicks was considered one of the preeminent sportscasters of his generation, calling a variety of high-profile events including the Olympics, PGA Tour and Notre Dame football. After beginning his career at CNN, Hicks had been at NBC since 1992. He was a tower announcer for the network’s golf coverage until being promoted to the lead play-by-play role in 2000. Among his most famous moments on the air, Hicks called Tiger Woods’ dramatic putt to force a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open as well as the U.S. swim team’s stunning comeback at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. His partners in the booth included Johnny Miller and Rowdy Gaines. “Dan Hicks was an extraordinary colleague, friend and person,” NBC Sports’ Rick Cordella, Sam Flood and Molly Solomon said in a statement. “In his 34 years at NBC Sports, he was an exceptional storyteller and caller of games and events who elevated some of the biggest moments in sports history. “From Olympic swimming and skiing to Notre Dame Football, numerous other high-profile events and especially as the signature voice of our golf coverage for the last 26 years, Dan’s blend of knowledge style, enthusiasm and humor informed and entertained fans for decades. But far beyond his on-air excellence, Dan was a better person who welcomed teammates with a smile, a joke, or a word of encouragement, sometimes all three in the same sentence. Our heartfelt condolences and love to his wife Hannah and his daughters Hannah, Ellery and Riley.”

item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 8: Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Crystal Palace FC and Liverpool FC at Selhurst Park on November 8, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. Mauricio Pochettino looks to be Carrick’s replacement at United and the club will have to pay U.S. Soccer $10M to get the manager out of his contract with the federation. item.description: For the third time, Camila Barros joins Brazil women's coaching staff São Paulo will have another representative with the Brazilian Women’s National Team for its final fixtures of 2026. Alongside defender Tayla, fitness coach Camila Barros will join Arthur Elias’s coaching staff for the friendlies against Japan. The matches will take place on November 29 at Edion Peace Wing Stadium in Hiroshima and on December 5 at JFE Harenokuni Stadium in Okayama. This is Camila’s third call-up. Her first stint with the national team came in February 2025, during a training camp at Granja Comary in Rio de Janeiro state. She rejoined the staff in October 2026 and now has another opportunity to contribute to the national team. “Working with the Brazilian National Team is a great learning opportunity, especially during this period of preparation for the World Cup. I see these stints as a chance to further develop my skills and bring that experience back to the club,” she emphasized. Camila’s journey with the Tricolor began in 2017, when the club partnered with Centro Olímpico to compete in the São Paulo State Under-17 Championship. An Under-15 team was also formed at the time and won the state title. Following that work, the coaching staff and players were brought into São Paulo’s youth setup on a permanent basis. Camila started as a fitness coach in the club’s youth ranks, working with the Under-16 and Under-17 teams from 2017 to 2021 and the Under-20 team in 2022. That same year, she joined São Paulo’s senior women’s team, where she has won major titles, including the 2025 Women’s Super Cup and the 2026 Brazilian Women’s Championship. For her, those achievements helped open doors. “The work done by both the Health and Performance Department and the coaching staff was crucial to my call-ups. I believe the great work we have been building year after year, with important titles along the way, helped me earn these call-ups,” she said. Credits: Luan Ryder / São Paulo FC 2027 Women’s World Cup Brazil will host the Women’s World Cup for the first time, also marking the competition’s debut in South America. The tournament will run from June 24 to July 25, 2027, featuring 32 national teams, 64 matches and eight host cities: Belo Horizonte, Brasília, Fortaleza, Porto Alegre, Recife, Rio de Janeiro, Salvador and São Paulo. Camila also highlighted the excitement surrounding the country’s hosting of the tournament. “I believe everyone involved in women’s football, especially in Brazil, is eager to see this major event take place in our country, with the chance to watch top national teams play up close. item.description: Rory McIlroy laid down an early marker in his pursuit of a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai crown, finishing strongly to sign for a three-under-par 69 at the DP World Tour Championship . The Northern Irishman produced a magnificent fairway wood from 255 yards at the final hole to set up a 13-foot eagle attempt. Although he left the putt short, the resulting birdie capped a fine opening round. That late flourish lifted McIlroy into a share of third place, three strokes clear of playing partner Eugenio Chacarra. The Spaniard narrowly avoided serious damage on the 18th when his drive struck a rock near the creek, bouncing safely over the water to allow him to salvage a par five. Despite sitting down in 23rd position after the opening day, the 26-year-old Spaniard still leads the projected seasonal standings, though he can ill afford to let his main rival gain much more ground. On a testing, breezy day at the Earth Course, McIlroy ended the day two shots adrift of leader Joost Luiten. He was one of just two players among the top nine in the Race to Dubai rankings to break par in the challenging conditions. McIlroy is firmly in the mix after the opening round (Getty) Jon Rahm , triumphant last week, was the other, shooting a one-under 71. Meanwhile, Patrick Reed ’s ambitions took a severe blow after the American, third in the standings, carded a three-over 75 to end up down in 41st place. It was a mixed round for McIlroy, who three-putted twice on the front nine despite making three birdies and a bogey. He delivered when it mattered most at the last, capitalizing on the fact that Chacarra was unable to reach the green in two by hitting his approach onto the putting surface to secure a closing birdie. "Very pleased. It was tricky, windier than it usually is and with the more punishing rough this week and cross winds, I felt I did well to hit fairways," said the world number two, who is bidding to match Colin Montgomerie’s haul of eight Order of Merit titles. "Anything in the 60s today I felt was a good score. Held it together when I needed to and in a good position going into the rest of the week." McIlroy can claim the season-long crown if he wins on Sunday, or if he finishes second provided neither Chacarra nor Reed takes victory.
